parameters.content:
## Trigger & Idea Fetch

This section initiates the workflow on a scheduled basis and retrieves content ideas marked as “idea” from the database. It then processes each topic individually using a loop, enabling scalable handling of multiple content ideas in a structured and controlled manner.

## Processing Lock & Validation

This section ensures that each topic is marked as “processing” to prevent duplicate execution. It validates whether the topic meets minimum criteria before AI generation begins, ensuring only meaningful and non-empty inputs are passed into the content generation pipeline.

## Blog Generation

This section focuses only on generating the primary SEO blog using AI and validating its output. It ensures the blog content is successfully created before proceeding to downstream steps like social media generation, maintaining a strong foundation for all derived content.

## Social Content Generation

This section converts the generated blog into platform-specific formats. It creates a Twitter thread, LinkedIn post, and a supporting image, ensuring consistent messaging while adapting tone and structure for each platform’s audience.

## Centralized AI Error Handling
This section acts as a centralized error handling mechanism for all AI operations. If any AI node fails or produces invalid output, the workflow routes to this node, which sends a Slack alert. This ensures immediate visibility and prevents faulty data from progressing further.

## Draft Storage & Approval
This section stores the generated content in Airtable and sends a Slack message for approval. The workflow pauses using a wait node until the user responds, enabling human-in-the-loop validation before proceeding to publishing or regeneration.

## Approval Decision Routing
This section processes the approval response received from Slack. Based on the action (approve or reject), the workflow routes execution accordingly and updates the database status, ensuring proper tracking of content lifecycle.

## Approved Content Scheduler

This section periodically checks for approved content using a scheduler. It fetches approved records and processes them individually, ensuring that content is handled efficiently and prepared for publishing without manual intervention.

## Approval Validation Gate

This section validates that approved content exists before entering the publishing pipeline. It prevents unnecessary execution and ensures that only valid, ready-to-publish data proceeds to the next stage, improving workflow efficiency and reliability.

## Multi-Channel Publishing (Parallel Execution)
This section handles publishing content across multiple platforms in parallel. Each node independently pushes content to its respective platform, ensuring efficient and scalable distribution without blocking other publishing operations.

## Post-Publish State Update

This section synchronizes all parallel publishing operations using a merge node. Once all publishing tasks are completed, it updates the database status to “published”, ensuring accurate tracking only after all channels have successfully finished execution.

## Rejected Content Scheduler & Fetch
This section runs on a schedule to identify content marked as rejected in the database. It retrieves all such records and processes them individually using a loop, ensuring that each rejected item is re-evaluated and prepared for improvement without manual intervention.

parameters.content:
## Rejected Content Validation & Processing Lock
This section prevents duplicate processing by marking rejected records as “processing.” It then validates whether the topic or content is still usable for regeneration. This ensures only valid and necessary records enter the AI regeneration pipeline, improving efficiency and avoiding redundant executions.

## AI Regeneration Pipeline
This section enhances previously rejected content using AI. It regenerates the blog with improved quality and recreates platform-specific content such as Twitter threads and LinkedIn posts. This iterative process helps refine content until it meets approval standards.

## Save Regenerated Content
This section stores the improved content back into the database, replacing or versioning the previous rejected content. It ensures that the latest regenerated output is available for review and maintains consistency across the workflow.

## Re-approval Request & Wait
This section sends the regenerated content back to stakeholders via Slack for another review cycle. The workflow pauses and waits for user input, enabling human validation before deciding whether the improved content is ready for publishing.

## Re-approval Decision Handling
This section processes the response from the re-approval step. Based on user action, it updates the content status as approved or rejected again. This ensures that regenerated content follows the same quality control process before moving to publishing or further iteration.

## Centralized AI Error Handling
This section acts as a centralized error handling mechanism for all AI operations. If any AI node fails or produces invalid output, the workflow routes to this node, which sends a Slack alert. This ensures immediate visibility and prevents faulty data from progressing further.

## Workflow Overview & Setup Guide

This n8n workflow automates an end-to-end content marketing engine, transforming raw ideas into multi-platform campaigns. It begins by fetching topics from Airtable and uses OpenAI (GPT-4o) to generate a high-quality SEO blog, a 10-tweet thread, and a LinkedIn post, alongside an AI-generated image. To ensure quality, the workflow pauses and sends an approval request to Slack. Once a user clicks Approve, the content is published simultaneously to WordPress, Twitter, and LinkedIn. If Rejected, the AI automatically improves the draft and restarts the approval cycle.

**Setup Steps:**

**1.** Airtable Base: Create a table named "Content" with fields for Topic, Status (Options: idea, processing, pending_approval, approved, rejected, published), Blog, Twitter, LinkedIn, ImageURL, and Version.

**2.** API Credentials: In n8n, configure credentials for OpenAI, Slack, Airtable, WordPress, and Twitter/LinkedIn using your respective API keys or OAuth tokens.

**3.** Slack Integration: Create a Slack channel for approvals and update the Channel ID in all Slack nodes within the workflow.

**4.** Webhook Accessibility: Ensure your n8n instance is accessible via a public URL so the Wait nodes can successfully receive the "Resume" signal from the Slack approval buttons.

**5.** Trigger Configuration: Activate the workflow and adjust the Trigger: Generate Content node to your preferred schedule (e.g., once per day or hour).
